content.p: On 9 June 2024 a body with multiple injuries was found beside a stormwater drain next to an apartment block in Sumanahalli, in west Bengaluru. It was later identified as Renukaswamy, a 33-year-old from the town of Chitradurga who worked for a pharmacy company. Within two days, police had arrested one of the biggest stars of Kannada cinema, the actor Darshan Thoogudeepa, along with his partner Pavithra Gowda and others. Police say Renukaswamy, a fan of the actor, was killed after he sent obscene messages to Gowda.

More than two years on, nobody has been convicted. A Bengaluru court framed charges against 17 people on 3 November 2025, and all of them pleaded not guilty. The trial is in progress, Darshan is in judicial custody, and a fight over whether one of the accused may testify for the prosecution has now reached the Supreme Court. Everything below about how Renukaswamy died is the prosecution's account, as given by police and put to the courts. It has not been tested to a verdict.

Police said a food delivery boy who noticed dogs eating a human body raised the alarm. The News Minute, citing police, wrote that a security guard found it. The post-mortem report, as cited by police sources, gave the cause of death as shock and haemorrhage resulting from multiple blunt injuries, and police said there were multiple fractures across the body.

Renukaswamy's wife, Sahana, said a man named Raghavendra picked up her husband from near their house on a Friday night. Police say Raghavendra was the Chitradurga convenor of Darshan's fan club and had gathered information on the victim. The News Minute dated the abduction to 8 June 2024.

According to police sources quoted by The South First, Renukaswamy had commented on Gowda's social media account, saying she had caused a split between the actor and his wife, and used indecent language. Police said Gowda instigated Darshan to punish him and that a plan was then hatched. The News Minute reported the police version that Darshan wanted to teach Renukaswamy a lesson and conspired with fans to abduct him.

Police said the victim was taken to a shed in the Kamakshipalya area of Bengaluru. The News Minute described it as a shed used for parking seized vehicles. Police sources said Darshan beat him with a belt, that he was then beaten with sticks after he collapsed, and that he was thrown against a wall, which proved fatal. A separate account says the investigation found he had been branded with hot metal and given an electric shock. Police named one accused, Dhanaraj, as the man who allegedly administered the shocks, and said they seized an "electric shock torch" from his home. The body was then dumped in the drain.

Darshan has denied the charges. His lawyer Ranganath Reddy told the BBC in June 2024 that the police had no direct evidence against the actor and that it was "a case of circumstantial evidence". Gulf News wrote in 2026 that Darshan and several others have denied wrongdoing.
content.h2: Arrests, a surrender and the money
content.p: The Indian Express reported that Darshan was arrested on 11 June 2024, together with Gowda and 11 others, and that three more people were arrested afterwards. The South First wrote that two accused came forward to Kamakshipalya police during the investigation and "confessed" to killing Renukaswamy over a financial dispute. The Hindu reported, citing police, that an accused named Deepak had reportedly handed ₹5 lakh each to four men who surrendered in order to protect Darshan, with ₹30 lakh promised to each.

The prosecution told the court in June 2024 that it had recovered ₹30 lakh paid to the family of one accused. By September 2024, police said Darshan, in a revised statement, had admitted obtaining ₹40 lakh from a friend, Mohan Raj, to escape legal action and to cover up the conspiracy. Police said ₹37.4 lakh was recovered from his house and ₹3 lakh from his wife. The statements were reported through police briefings and have not been tested at trial.
The BBC noted that police were officially giving out few details, while the local press ran allegations attributed to police sources. Blurry CCTV footage shown on television channels was one example.

On 4 September 2024, Bengaluru City Police Commissioner B. Dayananda announced that a 3,991-page chargesheet had been filed against 17 accused before the 24th Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate. He said it named 231 witnesses, 27 of whom had made statements before a magistrate, and that 56 police personnel were among the witnesses. He said all 17 accused had been arrested. Pavithra Gowda is accused no. 1 and Darshan is accused no. 2. Police sources said she was the "major cause" and had instigated the others, claims that remain allegations.

On 10 September 2024 the Karnataka High Court issued a gag order restricting media from publishing details of the chargesheet, The News Minute reported. On 24 November 2024 police filed a supplementary chargesheet of about 1,300 pages, which was said to contain more technical evidence.

After nearly four and a half months in judicial custody, Darshan received six weeks of interim bail from the High Court on 30 October 2024 for spinal surgery, on condition that he surrender his passport and furnish a bond of ₹2 lakh. In November the Karnataka government alleged he had not followed his bail conditions. The High Court granted regular bail to Darshan, Gowda and five others on 13 December 2024.

The State challenged that order. On 14 August 2025 a Supreme Court bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and R. Mahadevan cancelled the bail, calling the High Court order "perverse" and "wholly unwarranted", and saying it had been passed "in a mechanical manner". The judges said the High Court had weighed witness statements, a job for the trial court. In July the bench had remarked that the order "basically dictated an acquittal". Justice Pardiwala said "no man is above the law" and warned that if the accused were given "five-star treatment" in jail, the jail superintendent would be suspended. The court said Darshan would be lodged in Bengaluru's Parappana Agrahara prison. Renukaswamy's father, Shivanagouda, told PTI that the family's faith in the judiciary had grown.

When the accused were brought before Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge I.P. Naik on 3 November 2025, the courtroom was so packed that proceedings moved to a closed chamber. The court framed charges of murder, criminal conspiracy, kidnapping and unlawful assembly. All 17 pleaded not guilty, and the trial was set to begin on 10 November.

By May 2026 progress was slow. A report from the trial court told the Supreme Court that in the seven months since charges were framed the prosecution had examined 10 witnesses out of 272 listed. On 15 May 2026 the bench of Justices Pardiwala and Vijay Bishnoi refused Darshan bail. It directed that 60 important witnesses be examined within a year, allowed day-to-day hearings, and told the State not to keep "multiplying witnesses". The bench also directed that Darshan receive every amenity an undertrial prisoner is entitled to under the prison manual. If there was no substantial progress after a year, it said, he could apply again. Darshan's counsel, Mukul Rohatgi, had argued for bail on the ground of delay, while the State's counsel, Siddharth Luthra, said the examination in chief had been completed in a day and the defence then took five or six days over cross-examination.

On 24 June 2026, Deccan Herald reported, Darshan asked the Supreme Court to clarify that its order was not an absolute bar on any court considering bail if circumstances changed, such as continued delay or medical need.

On 30 June 2026 a prosecution witness told the court he had received threatening phone calls instructing him how to depose. Deccan Herald reported on 2 July that three men from Tumakuru, an administrator, an editor and a member of a Facebook fan page called "D Company", were arrested for allegedly threatening the witness, and were sent to police custody for five days.

In August the State went to the High Court after the trial court refused its request to question the first prosecution witness, the victim's mother, partly under Section 154 of the Evidence Act, without declaring her hostile. The prosecution said call records showed calls of 27 and 47 seconds between her phone and her son's on the date of the incident, which it said contradicted her testimony. Justice M. Nagaprasanna reserved his order on 12 August after hearing Darshan's counsel argue that she was not hostile and had merely made admissions in cross-examination.

Pradosh S. Rao, accused no. 14, applied to turn approver, offering what he called a full and truthful disclosure about the murder and the roles of the co-accused. The prosecution consented. On 13 August 2026 the High Court dismissed Darshan's petition against the trial court's refusal to let him file objections, holding that co-accused have no right to be heard at that stage. On 25 August the trial court granted Rao a conditional pardon. Among the conditions, he must make a full and true disclosure and stay in custody until the trial ends; if he conceals anything or lies, he can be tried as an accused again. On 27 August Rao's counsel told the court he was facing "severe pressure" and wanted to be examined quickly. Counsel for two other accused, Ravi Shankar and Vinay, said their clients also meant to apply for approver status, Deccan Chronicle reported.

Examination was fixed for 2 September but deferred while Darshan's challenge was pending. On 8 September Justice Nagaprasanna set aside the trial court's orders of 20 and 25 August, citing "procedural aberrations", and sent the application back for a fresh order without a fresh hearing. Telangana Today reported on 29 September that the trial court was recording Rao's statement, that it ran for nearly three hours in camera on a Monday, and that Darshan and his wife, Vijayalakshmi, had filed three petitions in the Supreme Court. That report also says the High Court had upheld the grant of approver status, which conflicts with the 8 September order reported by LiveLaw and by Telangana Today itself; the two accounts have not been reconciled in reporting.

On 18 September 2026 the High Court, on a petition filed on Darshan's behalf by his wife Vijayalakshmi, ruled on whether Darshan must be physically brought to court. The trial court had refused this on 17 August and offered video links. The High Court said the prosecution must examine 60 witnesses, that Darshan could be produced in person when material witnesses are cross-examined but not during their examination in chief, and that cross-examination could be held in camera. It said the order should not be treated as a precedent.

No verdict has been delivered. The prosecution has about 272 witnesses on its list, and Deccan Herald reported that Darshan's side puts the number to be examined at around 262. The Supreme Court said on 15 May 2026 that it would watch the trial for one year before looking at bail again. Darshan remains in custody and Pavithra Gowda and the other accused are charged, not convicted.
